title: The mysterious
hook: Einstein wrote that the most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious

segments.voice: Yesterday, Darwin's entangled bank, and grandeur in weeds and worms. Your line was endless forms most beautiful. Today, a physicist names what he thinks is worth the most.

What's the most beautiful thing a person can experience? Ask around and the answers come quickly. A newborn's face. A sunrise over water. Falling in love. A piece of music that stops you halfway up the stairs. Albert Einstein, the physicist, gave a different answer in an essay about what he believed: the most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious. Not the solved. The mysterious.
screen: `THE MOST BEAUTIFUL THING?` → `A PHYSICIST'S ANSWER.` → `NOT THE SOLVED.`

segments.voice: His words are paraphrased here, not quoted. First, the claim. The most beautiful thing we can experience, Einstein wrote, is the mysterious. Not a puzzle waiting for an answer key, but something real we can sense and can't get to the bottom of. Second, where it leads. He called it the source of all true art and all true science. That's a surprise from a scientist. Plenty of people picture science as a machine for getting rid of mystery. He says the opposite: mystery is where the work begins, and where it keeps coming from. Third, what happens without it. A person to whom this feeling is a stranger, Einstein wrote, who can no longer pause to wonder and stand rapt in awe, is as good as dead: their eyes are closed. Strong words. Fourth, his religion. Knowing that something we can't penetrate exists, a deep reason and a radiant beauty our minds can grasp only in their most basic forms, is at the heart of true religiousness, he went on. Then he drew a careful line: in that sense, and in that sense only, he counted himself among the devoutly religious. He was naming his own meaning of the word, not setting a rule for anyone else's.
screen: `THE MOST BEAUTIFUL THING` · `THE SOURCE OF ART AND SCIENCE` · `EYES THAT CAN STILL WONDER` · `RELIGIOUS IN THIS SENSE ONLY` · then, large: `THE MYSTERIOUS.`

segments.voice: Choose one thing you can't explain and probably never will: why music can move someone to tears, what another person's inner life is really like, why the world can be understood at all. Hold it the way you'd hold a stone in your palm, without trying to solve it. When the mind starts arguing, set the argument down and go back to simply holding the question.
The mysterious. Einstein's name for what we sense but can't get to the bottom of, which he called the most beautiful thing we can experience. Today's word.
Your line: stand rapt in awe. Not the solved, the mysterious. Day one thousand twenty-five, done.

howItsDone: Some people on a personal spiritual path, religious and not, keep a practice of sitting with an open question rather than an answer, and Einstein's essay is often read as a description of that kind of wonder.

notes: Einstein is paraphrased throughout: English translations of the essay are not on the public-domain list (and the US status of the 1930s translations should be checked before any quotation).

Paraphrase follows the essay: the mysterious as the most beautiful thing we can experience; the source of all true art and science; one to whom the emotion is a stranger is as good as dead, eyes closed; knowledge of what we cannot penetrate, the profoundest reason and most radiant beauty, at the center of true religiousness; 'in this sense, and in this sense alone' he counts himself devoutly religious. Confirm against the German.
Original: 'Das Schönste, was wir erleben können, ist das Geheimnisvolle.' Confirm spelling and the pronunciation guide.
'People of many faiths mean more than that by religion' is meant to avoid presenting Einstein's definition as the definition; confirm it is fair and unranked.
Outline date (1930) left out under the claims rule; the hook keeps the outline's 'most beautiful' because the cited essay says it.
